Accepted predecessor Stata handoff metadata: attempt_05/data/reg.dta has 63,193 rows and 99 columns; case-sensitive fyear is int16 and datadate is retained. Fresh work/data/reg.dta has 71,738 rows and 99 columns; lower-case fyear is int16, and controller isid gvkey fyear passed.

Paper Table 5 and assigned predecessor results: local papers/pdf/W3126118385.pdf physical pp. 17–19; output/reproductions/packages/W3126118385/attempt_05/outcome.json and its three aggregate Model 1 tables/native notebook outputs.
changes: Pooled the original FY1989–FY2005 window with attainable FY2006–FY2008 observations. Raw support is FY1984–FY2009 so the original t−5 history and one-year FY2009 lead remain available; requested endpoint remains FY2010.

Derived the FX source bound from actual non-USD FY2009 reporting dates of FY2008 firms; latest required DATADATE is 2010-05-31. Current daily and monthly sources support the screened FY2009 leads with exact pairs.

Extended the accepted 37% MTR construction branch through FY2009 for the needed FY2008 lead; this is an explicit assumption because the paper schedule ends in FY2005 and accepted code previously used it through FY2006.

Kept the original Table 5 Model 1 formulas, proxy classifications, OLS commands, firm/year clustering, and pooled winsorization approach. Added an aggregate annual SAS eligibility audit and Stata e(sample)-based original/added counts without changing observation-level rows.

Limited supported analysis years to FY1989–FY2008 because the current standard-filtered Compustat source has one unresolved FY2010 firm-year key with two reporting dates, and accepted code specifies no tie rule.
limitations: The requested FY2010 endpoint is not reached. FY2010 has one duplicate GVKEY–FYEAR key with two distinct reporting dates; FY2011 has another duplicate key with two reporting dates. The accepted construction aborts on the first conflict and documents no vintage rule. These keys block FY2009 and FY2010 analysis outcomes, so the last complete continuous analysis year is FY2008 with FY2009 as its lead.
No source row was selected or dropped to resolve the FY2010 or FY2011 conflicts.

The paper states a 37% marginal tax rate only through FY2005; accepted build code extended that rate through FY2006 for the original lead. Reusing 37% through FY2009 is a documented continuation assumption, not verified year-specific statutory-rate data.

The accepted reconstruction baseline had smaller samples than the paper (26,242 CF; 17,713 A&R; 26,438 age versus 48,369 reported). The extension preserves complete-case definitions and inherited IDIT/IINT mapping and construction assumptions; it does not tune screens to published N.

The fresh CF-pattern and A&R clustered runs report a non-positive-semidefinite VCV adjustment and no model F statistic with 20 fiscal-year clusters. Their coefficient tables and native logs are retained; no alternative covariance estimator was substituted.

The source Table 5 prints total stage effects and tests increments from reference groups. The accepted output convention prints indicator contrasts in the aggregate table and prints total effects via lincom in the native log. Comparisons identify which measure is used.

Inherited best-effort limitations remain: IDIT as a semantic proxy for unavailable IINT; CRSP PERMCO market-equity substitution; unspecified fiscal averaging, A&R timing/ties, zero-sign handling and winsorization pool; and the four-input A&R 4–12 arithmetic range despite the paper’s 3–9 wording.
